about: The Curse of Alduin: lore, and the trials every city's Echo Altar sets before it wakes. At the altar the player picks any three of the five trials (trials), in any order; when three are done the city's Barrow-Jarl (bosses, by town) rises near the altar at night, and slaying it frees the city. Each trial's n and seconds are given per Skyrim difficulty, Novice to Legendary (iDifficulty 0-5). Progress lives in one global per city (1000000 + doneBits*100000 + active*10000 + progress, 9000000 = freed), saved with the game. {city} is filled per city, {n} and {s} with the trial's count and seconds. A freed city is a sanctuary: no undead rise within zoneRadius of its station or in its own location; its shout waits at the altar.
prologue: Helgen burned, and you lived. But Alduin did not flee: as he rose from the ash he shouted three words into the earth - GRAH DIR LEIN, Battle, Death, World - and every barrow in Skyrim answered. Now when the sun goes down the dead claw their way up to finish what he began. Only the Echo Altars the ancient Tongues raised in every hold can still his voice, and they have gone dark. Wake them, city by city, and their dead will sleep again.
liftedText: The altar of {city} rings with the old Tongues' answer, and Alduin's voice falls silent here. Its dead sleep again: none will rise within its bounds.
freedAll: Every Echo Altar in Skyrim is awake. Alduin's voice lingers only in the wild places, and it will not fall silent until the World-Eater does.

trials.title: Ward of the Tongues
trials.short: Hold the runic circle at the altar
trials.goal: Stand in the runic circle at the Echo Altar of {city}
trials.text: The Tongues who raised the Echo Altar of {city} sealed it with a circle of runes that only a living voice can hold open. Stand inside it while Alduin's echo drives the dead against you, thicker than any night before; step out and the runes fall quiet until you return. Hold the circle for {s} seconds.

trials.title: The Culling
trials.short: Slay the risen before the echo swells
trials.goal: Slay the risen within {city} before time runs out
trials.text: GRAH - Battle. The first of Alduin's three words calls the dead to war, and the altar answers war with war. Put {n} of the risen down within {city} before {s} seconds pass, or the echo swells again and the count starts over.

trials.title: The Unbroken
trials.short: Slay the risen without falling below half health
trials.goal: Slay the risen within {city} without falling below half health
trials.text: DIR - Death. Alduin's second word feeds on the wounded. Slay {n} of the risen in {city} without letting your health fall below half; bleed past it and the count begins again.

trials.title: Trial of Steel
trials.short: Slay the risen in melee alone
trials.goal: Slay the risen within {city} with blade, axe, mace or fist
trials.text: The Barrow-Jarls ruled by the sword, and the old dead respect nothing else. Put {n} of the risen in {city} down in melee - no spell, no bow, no Thu'um counts.

trials.title: The Long Night's Breath
trials.short: Survive the waves that rise round the altar
trials.goal: Survive the waves that rise round the Echo Altar of {city}
trials.text: LEIN - World. The last word is Alduin breathing the world back into his dead. {n} waves will claw up round the altar of {city}, each stronger than the last. Clear each one before {s} seconds pass, or the barrow breathes out again and the wave doubles.

Riverwood.name: Skjold Barrowborn
Riverwood.text: Skjold was laid in Bleak Falls Barrow before Riverwood had a name, a jarl of the first Nords who swore he would hold the valley forever. Alduin took him at his word. He rises from the river mist to keep the altar silent.

Whiterun.name: Jarl Ulfgar the Bone-Crowned
Whiterun.text: Before Dragonsreach there was Ulfgar, who ruled the plains from a hall of turf and wore the skulls of his rivals as a crown. Grah Dir Lein woke him under the Gildergreen's roots, and he means to rule Whiterun again.

Solitude.name: The Wolf Queen's Shade
Solitude.text: Potema Septim raised the dead of Solitude once in life and was sealed beneath the city for it. Alduin's word slipped through the seal. What rises is not the queen but her hunger, still calling the dead to her court.

Windhelm.name: Vrolund Ice-Hand
Windhelm.text: Vrolund held Windhelm's gate in the Dragon War and froze the sea to keep the Atmorans' foes out. His barrow lies under the snow by the docks. His hand is still cold enough to stop a heart.

Markarth.name: The Briar-Heart King
Markarth.text: The Reach's oldest king cut out his own heart and grew a briar in its place, so that no blade could find it. The Forsworn forgot him; the dead did not. He climbs from the stone beneath Markarth to guard the altar.

Riften.name: Lady Hjaldis of the Black Mire
Riften.text: Hjaldis drowned herself in the Black Mire rather than yield Riften to the dragons, and the swamp kept her. When Alduin shouted, the mire gave her back - wailing, and with the fen's dead at her heels.

Falkreath.name: Hagla the Gravemother
Falkreath.text: Falkreath's graveyard is older than the town, and Hagla tended it when it was young. She buried every child of the hold, and now she wants them back. She rises from the oldest grave to keep them.

Morthal.name: The Drowned Jarl of Hjaalmarch
Morthal.text: Hjaalmarch's first jarl sank with his longship in the marsh and never rose - until Grah Dir Lein. He walks out of the fog bloated with black water, and the marsh's dead follow him.

Dawnstar.name: The Nightcaller Wight
Dawnstar.text: Once a priest of the Nightcaller Temple, the wight dreamed Alduin's return a thousand years before it came. It woke smiling. Kill it, and Dawnstar's nightmares end.

Winterhold.name: Archmage Valdrek the Collapsed
Winterhold.text: Valdrek fell into the sea with half of Winterhold in the Great Collapse, still casting. The storm he was raising never finished. Now it walks the cliff-tops in his bones, and it is not finished yet.
